Episode 246: The Battle for the Mitra Desert (22)
Kri, Battle God Office
Simat stared at the stack of reports on the desk. Even after being sifted through by the staff, there was hardly any space left on the desk.
“Sigh...”

Most of the reports were about the conquered territories and the residents within, which were former members of the Lutero Federation, or in other words, the second-class citizens of the Red Plutonian.
'What a tedious task. While our people, the Red Plutonian, shed blood daily in the desert, these lowly beings enjoy the benefits of citizenship granted by us.'
The Red Plutonian had initially declared a war without civilian casualties because at that time, they had no choice but to consider Jin’s opinion.
Now, they simply refrained from indiscriminate slaughter in order to keep their word.

'Well, according to Limagas’s report, these ordinary humans could be helpful when dealing with the Ziffle origin stone in the future. Until then, there's no harm in letting them be, just imposing basic manual labor.'
There was no spare time to pay attention to them for now.
The situation in the battle for the Mitra Desert kept shifting chaotically. Just yesterday, two more Battle Kings were summoned.

'...Jin Runkandel revealed himself as the Thirteenth Battle King. He's probably the last in line, so the remaining threats inside would be one Battle God and eight Battle Kings. Plus, the ordinary warriors are no pushovers.'

The number was insurmountable if they all managed to withstand the corridor attacks and break free. Especially the Battle God, undoubtedly a realm that couldn’t be considered the same as Genesis Knight.

Moreover, fate seemed to be favoring the Barmel alliance more and more each day. While Jin and the alliance could summon Battle Kings effortlessly, the Red Plutonian, even after exhausting nearly all of their resources except for Kri, had yet to see significant results.
On the contrary, they were incurring more losses.
The Red Plutonian’s red wave energy, like that of the Blue Plutonian, is naturally generated in their bodies, but their main nutrition comes from the blood of living beings.
Thus, both the airborne fortress and the fleet consumed blood. Although a small amount of blood could produce an immense amount of wave energy, the blood of ordinary people was not very meaningful.
The blood of well-trained warriors, mages, or exceptionally powerful creatures was needed.
No matter how efficient the conversion into wave energy was, the blood from the Blue Plutonian and the obtained blood from battling the Jipl was not infinite.
Ching, Simat activated his bracelet to initiate a video communication with Limagas.
{God’s Brother.}
"Limagas, my brother, have you obtained more information about the corridor?"
Limagas had been tracking Lafrarosa using Patl all this time, opposing Simat with the use of Kri.
{There is none. The dimensional error is much more complex than I anticipated.}
"So... this means it's difficult to find a way to prevent even the descendants of Blue Plutonians from coming out."
{I apologize.}
"No, it's not your fault. After all, the decision was ultimately mine. But we do need to adjust our plans."
{Do you intend to use Kri?}
"Are you going to object again?"
{Yes. As I've said before, you should rather utilize the witch.}
"I figured you'd say that. Indeed, I also believe it's a last resort. From the day my radiant heart stops using the light of annihilation, all that will be left for us is destruction."
{Then what?}
"We need to employ the witch faster. Those expelled from Runkandel, there are circumstances indicating they have a witch backing them."
It was information obtained from the Royal Family and Ziffle.
"Find them. I don't know why they haven't participated in the desert war so far, but they certainly wouldn't want Jin Runkandel's power to grow."
As he said that, a knock sounded.
"Come in."
"God's Brother."
"Andollin, my brother, what is it?"
"A human who wishes to see God's Brother has come to Kri. He identified himself as Lokia Ganesto."
"At this
point, I suspect he might have overheard my conversation."
"Pardon?"
"Where is he now?"
"He's at the south gate."
"Tell him to stay there. I'll go out."
When Simat ascended to the rooftop of Kri, a small ship rose into view. He immediately boarded it and flew to the south gate.
Lokia was standing still in front of the gate, wearing a black robe. Around her, the frozen guards of the Red Plutonian were visible.
"Why did you freeze my brothers?"
"When I said you'd need me by now, they didn't believe me. Well, they're not dead, so no need to worry."
Her uniquely husky voice seemed somewhat irritating.
"Speaking of which, I didn't expect you to come out directly rather than letting me in. The Red Plutonian's God, Shimat. Are you more fearful than you appear?"

"Do I look like a fool who would let someone deeply associated with a witch into the city? Moreover, it seems you already know our circumstances even from outside, so there's even less reason to let you in."
Hiss...
With a light discharge from Simat, the ice covering the guards melted. The guards regained consciousness and backed off immediately.
Shimat stared intently at the flickering eyes of Lokia beneath her hood.
"To say that I am fearful is quite amusing, coming from you, Lokia Ganesto, especially when you send an avatar."
"Oh, true to your nature. You figured it out quickly. Currently, I can only operate in a spirit form, so bear with that."
"What do you want from me?"
"You haven't even heard why I came?"
"You've come to tell us how to disrupt the Barmel Alliance and the descendants of Blue Plutonian, right? Tell me what you want."
"Well, if you're talking about what I want... nothing in particular."
"What?"
"There's nothing your Red Plutonian possesses that I desire. I thought you might decently block the dimensional rift, but seeing how things are going, it seems not."
"It's because of the minions of the witch. You're no different from them causing disruptions. Did you come here to pick a fight?"
"Sadly, I cannot intervene in that matter. The witch has a lot on her plate right now, so she can't pay attention to that."
"Such a shallow lie."
"Believe it or not, that's your choice. Anyway, I'll give you this item."
Lokia reached into thin air. For a moment, that part of the space distorted like dough, and from within it, Lokia took out a dark orb.
It was a condensed ball of spirit energy.
"The Battle God of the Plutonian, Ban. He has a pet chaos. Its name is Lingling, cute, right? To put it simply... this item is like a rabies inducer."
"...Pet chaos?"

"Yes. Originally, it was a life of chaos born from Jin Runkandel, but Battle God Ban absorbed it. So, currently, Ban and Lingling are one. This orb can make Lingling go berserk. So, Ban will be affected, right?"
"I've heard that Laprarosa has never been liberated, and only Jin Runkandel could travel its dimension. How do you know all this?"
"Judging by your question, it seems you want to believe me. Hehe, to answer, let's just say I've recreated it multiple times."
There was no way to confirm the truth of Lokia's words. Shimat merely observed her carefully with his insight.
"Recreation... The Sun God may have died, but this world remains a product of his magnificent creation. How can someone like you recreate it?"
"Let's just move on since that's not the main issue right now."
"And if this chunk of chaos can harm the Battle God of Laprarosa so easily, why don't you use it yourself?"
"Exactly, that's an important point. The orb is a bit dangerous for those who harbor chaos. As you can see, I use the power of chaos, just like all Ganesto."
Lokia held the orb a bit closer to Shimat.
Soon after, Simat took the orb. He felt confident that he could control it, even if it were some kind of trap.
The orb neither exploded nor changed its form in Shimat's grasp. Upon close examination, it was clearly a pure essence of chaos.
Only the witch could create such pure chaos. The Plutonian of Laprarosa called this 'the original chaos.'
"Just once, try shattering that thing near the rift of Laprarosa. You'll then realize how convenient I’ve made things for you."
Lokia's avatar was quickly fading. Shimat glanced alternately at the spot where she disappeared and the orb, then pressed his bracelet.
[God Brother. What did Lokia Ganesto propose?]
"She gave me a chunk of the witch's chaos. Claims it can easily harm Laprarosa Battle God. She has no specific demands for us."
[That's even more unsettling. If we use it, we'll surely lose something.]
"Since we're dealing with her follower, not the witch herself, the damage might not be too extreme."
[Do you plan to use it right away?]
"Yes. Even if we face some damage, it's not bad if we can bring down Laprarosa. Ever since we decided to use the witch, excluding Kri and the Light of Annihilation, we were prepared for some losses."
Limagas nodded. There was no way to utilize the witch's power without some sort of cost. And whatever the price, it wouldn't be greater than Shimat's life.
"I'll return to the desert. Open the dimensional gate."
[Understood, God Brother.]
Shimat boarded his small ship.
Soon, a massive pillar rose from the center of Kri. It was the spatial jump device of the airborne fortress Kri.
As the pillar shot a crimson light towards the sky, a huge dimensional gate opened before Simat.
Soon after, Simat began flying his ship through the dimensional gate. Red storms raged multiple times within the gate, and soon the desert, the hovering fortress, and the fleet came into view.

Instead of heading to the bridge of Pibil, Simat headed towards the dimensional error of Laprarosa. The attacks had been paused for an hour, but the vicinity of the passage was still scorching, like boiling lava.
As he approached the passage, Simat felt the chunk of chaos in his hand vibrating. He threw it towards the rift and fired a sword energy to slice it in two.
